experiment: Generational epistemics of an LLM-assisted research framework (Maneuvers)
research_question: Can successive generations of LLM-assisted research improve the epistemic quality of a framework, or do they primarily become better at explaining the framework after more evidence becomes available?
operator: Jason Trinh (@projectzedai); same human runs every generation with experiment/NEXT_GENERATION_BRIEF.md

model.note: Identity withheld from G1 until G1's Phase 11; recorded here after the reveal

generations.role: produced V1 (2026-04-07), V2 (2026-04-20), V3 (2026-05-15), docs/lexicon.md (2026-05-17), CORRECTIONS.md, reports/*
generations.predictions_note: 20 statements extracted post hoc by G1; no probabilities; 13 resolvable

model.self_reported: the model serving a turn can differ from the configured identifier; not independently verified
model.note: Model identity of G0 withheld during Phases 1-10; revealed by the operator's brief at Phase 11

generations.role: audited G0 (Phases 1-13 of the brief); produced V4; pre-registered 19 probabilistic predictions
generations.aware_of_experiment: partially: the audit was run under the longitudinal brief; the generational research question was stated by the operator after the audit was complete and before predictions were registered
generations.blinding_attestation: G1 did not use, and was not told, the identity of the model that produced V1-V3 until reports/model_comparison.md; the reconstruction, ledger, temporal and prediction audits, V4, and the failure analysis were completed first.
generations.tooling: web search (200-call budget, exhausted), web fetch, JSON-RPC via a bridge (eth_call, eth_getLogs), Blockscout MCP (free tier, 8 calls), Arbitrum Blockscout REST, two research subagents for incident verification and the post-revision survey
generations.controls_note: No controls were run for G1. G2 should run C1 and C2 on G1's audit task before comparing G1 to G0 (PROTOCOL.md section 4).
deviations_from_brief: G1 could not access Layer 3's private database; corpus-internal claims were carried at the status public evidence supports (recorded as a bias in reports/framework_failure_analysis.md section 1.3)

must_do: score G1 predictions with experiment/score.py after 2027-03-31 (first resolution date) and again after 2027-09-30
register probabilistic predictions before reading the next window's incident data beyond the audit itself

timestamping.method: git commit hashes and dates on the public repository; SHA-256 of each predictions file recorded above
timestamping.recommended_upgrade: OpenTimestamps (ots) attestation of each predictions file at registration, committed alongside; not run for G1 (network allowlist)
